title: Exploring a registry collaboration with The Cute Syndrome Foundation

sentences.text: At FamilieSCN2A Foundation, we support SCN2A families, while The Cute Syndrome Foundation supports SCN8A families.
Published research links both disorders to variants that make a protein do too much (gain of function) or too little (loss of function).
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that connection has confidence 0.46—below 0.5—and should be treated cautiously.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Dragonfly, Simons Searchlight and Citizen Health already include people with SCN2A-related disorders.
We could compare their approaches as a starting point, without assuming that existing resources or data can transfer unchanged.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help check whether normal EEG readings between seizures, cerebellar edema and paroxysmal vertigo also occur in SCN8A-related disorders, rather than treating gaps in recording as confirmed differences.
Before combining information, we should check which individual variants increase activity, impair activity or cause loss of function, including the ClinVar variants listed below.
Both disorders have published gain- and loss-of-function evidence, so we should avoid grouping every variant together.
This month, send one inquiry to The Cute Syndrome Foundation asking whether the International SCN8A Registry could include SCN2A-related disorders and what would need checking first.
Treat possible reuse across communities as a hypothesis to explore, not an established outcome.
Which ClinVar missense variants in SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN8A, KCNQ2, CACNA1A and GRIN2B cause gain versus loss of function?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired—less able to carry out their chemical task—or loss of function?
Could published functional measurements help resolve these questions variant by variant?
Dear The Cute Syndrome Foundation team,
I’m writing on behalf of FamilieSCN2A Foundation to explore a small collaboration.
Published research identifies gain-of-function variants in both SCN2A- and SCN8A-related disorders.
Could the International SCN8A Registry potentially include SCN2A-related disorders?
Could you help identify the checks needed before taking this further?
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of FamilieSCN2A Foundation
